perspective:
Vincent’s available information:

- He is Vincent Chinana, an Alaska Native mechanic. He knows Patrick Guzman as his long-time friend, a construction worker; they met as teenagers, share a blue-collar bond, and often collaborate using Vincent’s mechanical skills and Patrick’s construction expertise.
- At the diner, Vincent hears Patrick is considering a new construction venture to expand his business. Patrick says it seems like a good opportunity, that it is risky but worth it, and that he is still weighing options. Vincent expresses worry about financial security and suggests Patrick reconsider or delay until he has more information. Patrick says he appreciates the concern and will think it over.
- Days later, Vincent notices Patrick avoiding detailed discussions about the investment. At Patrick’s construction site, Vincent tells Patrick he feels Patrick is not telling him everything and that he feels betrayed. Patrick says it is complicated, that he did not want to worry Vincent with details, apologizes for not being more open, and agrees to sit down and explain everything.
- At Vincent’s garage, Vincent learns the investment situation is serious. Patrick tells him it has been tough and that he might lose a significant amount if it does not turn around soon. Vincent offers to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses. Patrick gratefully accepts the support.
- A month later, Vincent learns or observes that the venture might actually turn a profit. At the coffee shop, Patrick confirms it is starting to look up and says he is relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologizes for doubting Patrick earlier and proposes a joint venture. Patrick agrees and says they should work out the details.
- At Vincent’s house, Vincent and Patrick are optimistic about the joint venture. Vincent says their combined skills can make it a success and proposes starting a business plan, outlining every step carefully. Patrick agrees to cover all bases and set it up for success.

Vincent does not have access to anything beyond what he personally observed, heard, said, or was directly told in these interactions.
